clue.text: The Met Office?

blocks.note: surface reading: the Met Office is Britain's national weather forecasting service
setter's reading: the Met is the Metropolitan Police, London's police force, and this is its headquarters

explanation.surface: A question about the people who forecast Britain's weather.
explanation.walkthrough: The Met Office is the UK weather service, but the Met is also London's Metropolitan Police, whose headquarters is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Scotland Yard is the famous headquarters building of London's Metropolitan Police force.

clue.text: Criticised medium supporting religion? Not I!

indicators.note: 'Not I' tells you to drop the letter I from the word for religion
in a down clue, something supporting sits underneath, so it comes after the other piece

blocks.note: a world religion
MED is the standard abbreviation for medium, as on clothing labels

explanation.surface: Someone denies being a spiritualist medium who props up a faith.
explanation.walkthrough: ISLAM without its I gives SLAM, with MED placed below it to make SLAMMED.
explanation.definitionFit: To slam a play or policy is to attack it harshly in words, so slammed means criticised.

clue.text: Regularly relent after losing head

indicators.note: losing its head means the word's first letter is removed

blocks.note: to relent is to become less harsh

explanation.surface: Someone habitually gives in once they have been beheaded, an absurd image.
explanation.definitionFit: Something happening often happens many times at frequent intervals, which is what regularly suggests.

clue.text: Cassoulet cooked in hopeless endeavour

indicators.note: ingredients that are cooked are transformed and mixed, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: a French bean and meat stew, used for its letters

explanation.surface: A kitchen disaster: trying to make a French stew turns into a failed effort.
explanation.definitionFit: A lost cause is a project or campaign with no chance of success, a hopeless undertaking.

clue.text: Catch part of finger

blocks.note: first meaning: to catch or arrest a wrongdoer, informally
second meaning: the hard plate at the fingertip

explanation.surface: Catching something by grabbing it with the end of a finger.
explanation.definitionFit: Police informally nail a suspect when they catch him, and a nail covers each fingertip.

clue.text: Brie and yoga excited Jellystone Park resident

indicators.note: excited things are stirred up and agitated, so the letters are jumbled

blocks.note: the French cheese, used for its letters
taken as written

explanation.surface: A cartoon creature gets worked up about cheese and stretching exercises.
explanation.walkthrough: Yogi Bear, famous for stealing picnic baskets, is a Hanna-Barbera cartoon character.
explanation.definitionFit: Yogi Bear is the cartoon bear who lives in the fictional Jellystone Park and steals picnic baskets.

clue.text: Perch in river loves deserted spot

indicators.note: deserted means emptied out, so only the outside letters of the word remain

blocks.note: R is the map abbreviation for river
love is zero in tennis, which looks like the letter O; two of them here
the word with its middle removed

explanation.surface: A bird finds a lonely place to sit by a river it loves.
explanation.definitionFit: A roost is the place where a bird settles to rest, so it is a perch.

clue.text: Some chump in a foreign garment

indicators.note: 'some' points to a portion of the following words, the answer sitting inside them

blocks.note: the letters run across the word boundaries

explanation.surface: A fool abroad wearing some odd item of clothing.
explanation.definitionFit: A pinafore is a sleeveless dress or apron worn over other clothes, a type of garment.

clue.text: Grandma determined to head north for French city

indicators.note: in a down clue, heading north means reading upwards, so the word is written backwards

blocks.note: nan is an informal word for a grandmother
set on something means determined

explanation.surface: Granny is resolved to travel up to a city in France.
explanation.definitionFit: Nantes is a large city in western France on the river Loire.

clue.text: Witnessing American teetotal rock star taking drug

blocks.note: A is a common abbreviation for American
TT is the abbreviation for teetotal
E is slang for the drug ecstasy
Sting is the singer, formerly of The Police

explanation.surface: Watching a sober American rock musician who nevertheless takes drugs.
explanation.walkthrough: The drug is added before the star's name rather than placed inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Attesting means bearing witness to something, formally confirming you saw it happen.

clue.text: Board‘s agreements from Paris and Berlin

blocks.note: oui is French for yes
ja is German for yes, the agreement from Berlin

explanation.surface: A company's board reaches consensus with partners in France and Germany.
explanation.walkthrough: The word itself is said to come from combining the French and German words for yes.
explanation.definitionFit: A Ouija board is a lettered board used in seances to receive supposed messages from spirits.

clue.text: Threaten chaps and chapesses equally at first

indicators.note: 'at first' asks for the opening letter of each of the preceding words

blocks.note: chaps are men
the opening letters of three words

explanation.surface: Intimidate men and women alike, without favouring either sex.
explanation.definitionFit: To menace someone is to put them in fear with threats, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Theoretical pamphlet written by able seamen

blocks.note: AB is the abbreviation for able seaman, so two or more are ABS
a tract is a short pamphlet, often religious or political

explanation.surface: A speculative leaflet authored by sailors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Written by' places the pamphlet beside the sailors, after them.
explanation.definitionFit: Abstract ideas exist in thought rather than concrete reality, so they are theoretical.

clue.text: Briefly talk about Olympic event

indicators.note: briefly means cut short, so the final letter of the word is lopped off

blocks.note: to discuss is to talk about something

explanation.surface: A quick chat about a sporting contest at the Games.
explanation.definitionFit: Throwing the heavy disc is a field athletics contest held at every Olympic Games.

clue.text: Half of sketch revealed framework

indicators.note: taking half of a six-letter word means discarding its last three letters

blocks.note: taken as written
to let on is to reveal a secret

explanation.surface: Part of a drawing shows the underlying structure.
explanation.definitionFit: A skeleton is the supporting structure of a body or building, its basic frame.

clue.text: Satirises the French politician over statistical organisation

blocks.note: la is a French word for the
Member of Parliament
O is the cricket scorer's abbreviation for an over
the Office for National Statistics, the UK government's statistics body

explanation.surface: A French politician mocks the government's statistics office.
explanation.definitionFit: To lampoon someone is to ridicule them publicly through satire or caricature.

clue.text: Smashed no replica china

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Broken crockery that was the genuine article, not a copy.
explanation.definitionFit: Porcelain is fine ceramic ware, commonly called china after the country where it was first made.

clue.text: Quickly send away detectives before parking at church

blocks.note: DI is detective inspector; several are DIS
P is the sign for parking
taken as written
CH is the abbreviation for church

explanation.surface: Police officers are hurried off before finding a space at the church.
explanation.definitionFit: To dispatch a letter or messenger is to send it off promptly to its destination.

clue.text: Get rid of wicked, spiteful woman

blocks.note: to shed is to cast off
synonym

explanation.surface: An exhortation to banish wickedness and malice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wicked' seems to describe the woman, but it belongs with 'Get rid of' in the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A she-devil is an informal term for a cruel, malicious or vindictive woman.

clue.text: Badly aligns railway component

indicators.note: something done badly is botched, so the letters end up in the wrong order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone does a poor job of lining up a part of the track.
explanation.definitionFit: Signals are the lineside devices that tell train drivers whether to stop or proceed, part of railway equipment.

clue.text: Politicians confused genres

blocks.note: taken as written

clue.text: Singer very expert, holding a note

blocks.note: so, as in so good, means very
a pro is a professional or expert
taken as written

clue.text: Perhaps gorilla seen in reportedly dull video

blocks.note: grey means dull, and a videotape is a video

clue.text: Is rodent turning up bones?

blocks.note: taken as written
a rat is a rodent

explanation.surface: Is a rodent digging up bones?

clue.text: Delayed assistance protects leader of Dundee United

indicators.note: to protect is to surround and shield, so one word goes around the other letters
the leader of a word is its opening letter

blocks.note: synonym
the first letter of the Scottish city
U is the standard abbreviation for United in football club names

explanation.surface: Help arrives late but shields the captain of the football club Dundee United.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dundee United' reads as one Scottish football club, but only the first word is cut to its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Being held up means being delayed, as traffic or a meeting can be.

clue.text: Hang the pardoned revolutionary guards

blocks.note: the letters straddle the two words

explanation.definitionFit: To drape a cloth is to hang it loosely over something, so it is a verb synonym.

clue.text: Stone or pearl, evenly cut

blocks.note: the first, third, fifth and seventh letters

clue.text: Answer second query, oddly missing affair

the second and fourth letters

clue.text: Best fruit for boss

clue.text: Renaissance man and logical men he upset

taken as written
